The title of the U.S. Code for diplomacy and foreign assistance. It holds the State Department's authorities, the Foreign Service, foreign aid, arms export controls, and most country-specific sanctions and policy statutes.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Current U.S. Code: 22 U.S.C. 1 et seq.](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/uscode/2024/title22){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Department of State organization and the Foreign Service, including chief of mission authority (sec. 3927).
- Foreign assistance (sec. 2151 and following) and arms export control (sec. 2751 and following).
- Participation in the United Nations (sec. 287) and registration of foreign agents (sec. 611).
- Country and issue statutes, including the Taiwan Relations Act, Cuba and Russia sanctions laws, human rights sanctions, and the Global Fragility Act.

## Why it matters

'Title 22' is shorthand for security assistance run by the State Department, in contrast to security cooperation run by the Defense Department under [Title 10](title10-usc.qmd). The two foundations of that system are the [Foreign Assistance Act](faa-1961.qmd) and the [Arms Export Control Act](aeca-1976.qmd).

## Current status

In force. Like Title 50 it is not positive law, so the underlying acts control.

## Where it sits

- **Layer.** Code title overview. Not a layer of authority but the shelf where enacted law is filed by subject. Titles 10 and 32 are themselves enacted law; Titles 22 and 50 are compilations. ([How the layers work](../study/index.qmd#the-authority-stack))
- **Codified in.** [Title 22 U.S.C.](title22-usc.qmd).
- **Era.** Interwar years and the Second World War ([timeline](../study/timeline.qmd)).
- **Study.** [Unit 1: Where the power comes from](../study/units/foundations.qmd) (further reading).
- **Member lenses.** [Rep. Sara Jacobs](../members/jacobs.qmd): Foreign Affairs.
